info.name: Shagan POS API
info.description: Generated from the API Endpoint Inventory doc. Every non-health route currently returns 501 until implemented.

request.description: Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY), not the regular bearer token - creates Organization + owner User + service_center User in one call. No Branch is created here; use POST /branches (as the owner) afterward, then POST /devices, then POST /internal/accounts/pos to attach a pos-type login to a device.

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Attaches a new pos-type User to an existing Organization + Device - device_id must already belong to org_id, otherwise returns 404 (not 403 - same not-found-not-forbidden reasoning as branches/staff/devices).

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Creates a Branch for org_id without needing an authenticated owner session - used right after CreateAccount, before the owner has ever logged in. Same validation/logic as the authenticated POST /branches, just with an explicit org_id instead of one read from the JWT.

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Registers a Device on branch_id without needing an authenticated owner session - branch_id must already belong to org_id, otherwise returns 404 (not 403 - same not-found-not-forbidden reasoning as the authenticated device/branch endpoints).

Short-lived elevation token for a single approval (void/return/manual-discount) - NOT for a manager's own backoffice sign-in, use VerifyStaffPIN for that. Requires a valid bearer access token (the calling device or owner) - :id is the staff being asked to approve, scoped to the caller's org (and branch, if the caller's own token carries one). permission is the specific permission code this approval is for (e.g. approve_void, approve_return, apply_manual_discount) - the target staff's role must actually grant it, checked via the same Roles/Permissions matrix as GET /roles/:id/permissions. Wrong staff, wrong branch, wrong PIN, and role-lacks-permission all return the same generic 401 (never 404) - a terminal can't enumerate staff IDs, branches, or role grants by probing. On success, returns the Staff record plus a separate 2-minute token (authtoken.StaffClaims) - much shorter than VerifyStaffPIN's 12-hour shift token, since this proves one momentary approval, not a signed-in session.

Cashier PIN sign-on at a terminal. Requires a valid bearer access token (the calling device or owner) - :id is the Staff being verified, scoped to the caller's org. If the caller's own token carries a branch_id (a pos-device token), the staff must belong to that same branch, otherwise this returns the same generic 401 as a wrong PIN (never 404) - a terminal can't be used to enumerate staff IDs or which branch they belong to. An owner/service_center token (no branch_id) can verify any staff in the org. On success, returns the Staff record plus a separate, shift-length staff-session token (12h TTL) - distinct from the caller's own device/owner access token.

Lists staff at this branch whose role grants the given permission code (query param, required) - not staff with role=manager specifically, since e.g. apply_manual_discount is granted to both super_staff and manager (see the v1 role/permission grant table). Use this to build a picker of who's eligible to approve a specific action before calling VerifyManagerPIN with the same permission code. An unrecognized permission code just returns an empty list, not an error.
